attempts.summary: Deployed a persistent host firewall on node1 via Ansible (run from control node node4), enforcing: SSH from anywhere, TCP/9000 accepted only from node2, and TCP/9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else. Implemented with firewalld direct rules (INPUT_direct chain, ordered by priority) because node1's firewalld 0.6.3 doesn't support rich-rule priority attributes, and firewalld zone rich-rule deny/allow chains otherwise evaluate reject before accept regardless of specificity. Verified persistence across a firewalld reload and across a full node1 reboot. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on all four nodes, one at a time, with boot-id proof and post-restart functional verification.
